snippet.textDisplay:
That’s the reason I like salary caps in sports - Only 4 clubs dominated in 20 over years? Obviously epl is still very entertaining to watch and I’m not saying there should be a salary cap, but theres hardly any stakes when being fan to a top team. You’re basically guaranteed to win every couple of years so the test of loyalty of being a fan isn’t really there. Being a fan of a middle/bottom table team must hurt because you’re really only competing with other middle/bottom teams and hoping for the occasional upsets against the big sides.

If you watch the NRL in Australia, when a team wins the competition, the players on that team will usually try and renegotiate their contract prices which a salary cap prohibits - this means if they want more money, they need to move to a different club that can afford them or the club itself needs to find a way to afford them. Overtime, this balances out the bottom/middle clubs with the top clubs so now this year has been pretty good. From 5th-17th are separated by 2-3 wins since the teams are almost even. A wooden spooner (bulldogs) 4-5 years ago is now leading the league since they had a full culture rebuild. A salary cap also incentivises the need of a junior academy - cheaper club depth is important so you can spend more money on big players. I wrote this out cuz I’m curious to see if anyone has an argument against a salary cap and give me a reason as to why it would be bad
